title: Phase and route resolution is computed in four places, bridged by an env var
problem: queue-loop.mjs:1085 says "Every routing choice is `decide()`'s". That is false: `nextRoute` holds routing rules, such as "a LAND on this head ends the review" and "a pinned ticket the owner relabelled is released", and `derive()` holds the phase table. `derive()` takes an injectable `exec` for gh, but git goes through a module-level `run` (loop-derive.mjs:18), so it is not injectable.
proposed: `readRun({cwd, base, worktree, ci, gh, git}) -> RunFacts`: I/O only. It returns `{ticket, branch, cwd, head, headSubject, commits, changed, dirty, comments|null, ci|null}`. `phaseOf(facts, handed?) -> {phase, why}`: pure, owning the table now at loop-derive.mjs:488-517.
effect: One home for the phase table. About 12 `derive(` calls and 17 env swaps in loopDerive.test.ts become table tests of `phaseOf`.

title: GitHub access is scattered, with about 7 argv-level gh fakes in tests and an unenforced `--repo` rule
problem: `tracker.mjs` is a real seam with two adapters (`ghTracker`, `fakeTracker`), but it covers only the 5 label and comment operations. Every other GitHub read is a hypothetical seam reached by argv, so each test re-creates gh's CLI semantics. The `--repo` rule is a premise held only in prose.
proposed: widen `tracker.mjs` into `github.mjs` with two adapters, `ghGitHub(gh = cli.gh)` and `fakeGitHub(state)`. Every adapter call appends `--repo REPO`, so the rule becomes structural. `fakeGitHub` grows from `fakeTracker` plus settleReplay's `rollupFake` state.
effect: About 15 call sites collapse to method calls. Tests deleted or replaced: 7 bespoke fakes become 1.
notes: Closed #1605/#1606 touched the loop adapter; 10-tests-e2e-loop confirms the argv-level fakes remain.

title: `queue-loop.mjs` is a god module: adapters, board glue, orchestration and config in one file
problem: the module's interface is everything it exports, about 40 names, and tests import about 30 of them. The real seam, `runOnce(ports, …)`, is buried among adapters that are themselves exported and tested one by one. The ports are not grouped by dependency.
proposed: `queue-loop.mjs` keeps only `runOnce(ports, events, pinned, at, loop)` and `main(deps)`. Ports regrouped by dependency category: `github`: `{ pick, facts, issueState, prFor(branch|ticket, {since, declared}), publish(n, branch, cwd), label(n, 'claim'|'release'|'park'), comment(n, file), settle(pending) }` — remote-owned/true-external. `workspace`: `{ stopFile, parkAsked(n), clearParkAsk(), sync(pinned), moved(), housekeeping(pinned), standing(), refresh(cwd, branch), buildPassed(cwd, n), sharedDirty(), …
effect: queue-loop.mjs drops from 1706 to about 500 lines; about 555 adapter lines go to `github.mjs`/`workspace.mjs`, about 190 board lines to `loop-board.mjs`, about 45 constant lines to `limits.mjs`, and about 90 routing lines go into `decide` (F2). Tests to delete: the duplicate `stubPorts` builder and the `place`/`OPTIONAL` machinery (one fake per port suffices).
notes: Closed #1605-#1608 (git/gh adapter, tracker port, settle stepper, runOnce ports) are possible partial progress; 10-tests-e2e-loop re-verified the stubPorts/io placeholders still real at queueLoop.test.ts:38-60 and queueLoopMain.test.ts:47-136. ADR-0004 (loop serialises) stands.

title: Policy and limits are spread over 8 modules; light scripts import the god module for one constant
problem: no single place answers "what are the run's caps". `decide()`'s input `limits` is built by its caller from four modules.
proposed: `limits.mjs` (already designated "plain constants, importable", limits.mjs:1) exports `LIMITS` and `SESSION_POLICY = {model, effort, context, turns, usd}`. `decide` defaults to `LIMITS`.
effect: decide.test.ts stops importing queue-loop.mjs; await-run and run-loop import a 30-line constants file; the stale comment goes.

title: `runOnce` and `main` bypass their ports for disk I/O, so tests `chdir`
problem: the composition's interface includes the process cwd and the real `.loop-logs`, while the ports suggest otherwise. `process.chdir` is process-global inside a concurrent test runner.
proposed: add `workspace.parkAsked(n)`, `workspace.clearParkAsk()`, `workspace.ciLog(n) -> path|null`, `ledger.logOf(n)` and `ledger.prune()` (see F1).
effect: 6 `chdir`s are deleted, and the class "a test touches the live loop record or cwd" goes away.

title: ci.yml's `scope` decision is inline bash, and its test regex-parses bash out of YAML
problem: the interface is YAML and bash, so the test reaches past it by parsing the implementation. The two path allowlists (ci.yml:131, 136) are the decision itself.
proposed: `tools/ci/scope.mjs` exporting `scopeOf(changed: string[]) -> {app, harness, scans}` and a CLI that prints `GITHUB_OUTPUT` lines. ci.yml keeps only the "identical tree already green" short-circuit and the `git diff`.
effect: about 75 lines of bash become about 40 lines of JS; ciScope.test.ts loses its YAML/regex extractor (lines 23-47) and calls `scopeOf` directly; scope becomes runnable locally.

title: `decide.mjs` exports its internals, and about 290 test lines test past `decide()`
problem: the interface is `decide(input)`, but the tests also pin the helper decomposition, so refactoring a helper breaks tests while behaviour is unchanged.
proposed: export only `decide`, `afterSession`, `WAIT` and `exhausted` (the last has a non-test caller in tools/ci/preflightMemory.mjs). Move the unique cases into decide.test.ts as `decide()` inputs.
effect: about 290 lines of queueLoop.test.ts deleted or converted; decide's interface shrinks from 13 exports to 4.

title: settle turns one transient gh error into an owner verdict
problem: Two cases become `verdict("owner","could not read CI")`: any single non-offline `gh` read error, and an offline error that no wake follows. So one transient 5xx parks the ticket for the owner, even though the settle machine already has a `stuck` bound that would let a retry happen.
proposed: Make the read error a retryable state inside `settle`'s pure machine, retried until the existing `stuck` bound and only then escalated to the owner. One branch, in the module that already owns the bound.
effect: Locality: the retry policy lives in one state table. Fewer owner escalations for noise.

title: The session environment is a hidden interface written in one place and parsed in five
problem: "am I a loop session?" is answered three different ways (`LOOP_TURNS` truthy, `LOOP_PHASE` matching a regex, `LOOP_TICKET` numeric). Production contract variables and test seams (`LOOP_BASE`, `LOOP_WORKTREE`, `LOOP_*_SCRIPT`) share one namespace. "Nothing in the loop may ever set" `LOOP_WORKTREE`/`LOOP_BASE` (loop-derive.mjs:411-418) is enforced only by prose; guard-bash has no rule about them.
proposed: `tools/loop/session-env.mjs`, the only module that names these variables: The test seams leave env: `derive`/`buildReady` take `{base, worktree}` parameters, which the gate's CLI could take as hidden flags, and `cli.mjs` exposes `withRunner(fn)` for tests instead of `LOOP_*_SCRIPT`.
effect: Six readers become `fromEnv()` calls. `clearLoopEnv.mjs` and `loopTestEnv.test.ts` become deletable once no production default reads env.

title: Process spawning is duplicated: the npm/npx shim, tree-kill, and the "run a bin" pattern, with a real orphan bug class on Windows
problem: five shallow copies of the same adapter. Each Windows `shell: true` site leaves orphaned trees on timeout or exit, which is the class `reap.mjs` and the memory notes exist to clean up.
proposed: `scripts/lib/proc.mjs` `cli.mjs`'s `run` and `queue-loop`'s `sh` delegate to it.
effect: About 9 call sites become calls into one module. Bug class removed: orphaned jest workers or servers after a timeout or exit on Windows.

title: Workflow duplication: installs, Node versions, and a byte-identical device gate
problem: shallow copies. A Node bump or an install change is about 20 edits. The soak job's production-Node pin carries no check.
proposed: `.github/actions/install` gains `node-version` defaulting to the repo version and an `npm-ci: always|cached` input for jobs that must not restore node_modules. `.github/actions/device-gate` (or `tools/ci/device-gate.sh`) replaces both gate jobs. Read production Node with `node-version-file`/`deploy/runtime.json` in soak.yml.
effect: About 13 install blocks become 1-line uses, and 9 literal Node versions become 0. deviceWorkflowsGate tests one script instead of two YAML extractions.
notes: 06-tooling: tooling-F9 is partly wrong: .github/actions/install already takes a required node-version input, so the proposal should be "default it from runtime.json", not "add an input". The rest holds (inline installs ci.yml:429-433, 519-523, 585-589, 956-975; literal Node 24 in five workflows; Node 22 in soak.yml; byte-identical gate jobs). 08-tests-rules-tooling-F18 confirms tooling-F6, F8 and F9.

title: Stale premises in prose and config
problem: loop-settings.json `soft_deny` says "package.json db:reset already bundles --yes". It does not: `db:reset` is `node scripts/reset-db.mjs && drizzle-kit push`, and reset-db refuses without `ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=1` and `--yes` (reset-db.mjs:15-40). So `npm run db:reset` can never succeed; it only prints `HOW_TO`.
proposed: correct the text; drop or rename `db:reset` to something like `db:reset:help`.
effect: Removes misleading premises.

title: Four scripts hand-roll the entry-point check
problem: `scripts/e2eBuildMark.mjs:33`, `scripts/mockupParityPage.mjs:162`, `scripts/ios-device.mjs:436` and `scripts/measureHeadsUpBalance.ts:556-557` compare unresolved paths. `scripts/lib/entry.mjs` (37 adopters) exists because that comparison breaks under junctions and subst drives.
proposed: use `isInvokedDirectly`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: loop-gate `landable` throws when a parent is not on main
problem: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1 for "not an ancestor". `landable` lets that throw, so the CLI exits 2 (crash) instead of reporting "not landable".
proposed: Treat exit 1 as false and rethrow only other codes.
effect: The gate gives an answer instead of a crash.

title: loop-screen `openExternally` has no spawn error listener
problem: The detached `spawn` has no `'error'` handler, so a missing opener binary raises an unhandled error and takes the supervisor's screen down with it.
proposed: Attach `.on('error', …)` and log.
effect: An optional convenience can no longer kill the loop.

title: claim.mjs leaks its mkdtemp directory
problem: The `mkdtempSync` directory is never removed, so one directory accumulates per claim.
proposed: Remove it in a `finally` block.
effect: Hygiene only.

title: e2ePort kills every listener on the chosen port, not the verified pids
problem: `clearPort(chosen.port)` lists the port again and kills whatever is listening by then, rather than the pids the claim verified. If a peer grabs the port in between, its server is killed.
proposed: Pass the verified pids through.
effect: Removes a cross-worktree race.

title: loop-logs ledger.record re-reads the whole ledger, which is never pruned
problem: Every `record` call parses the full append-only ledger, so the cost grows without bound.
proposed: Append without reading, or prune by age.
effect: Small; latent.

title: two definitions of a spec's duration
problem: One tool sums all attempts; the other takes the slowest attempt. They agree only because `playwright.config.ts:59` has `retries: 0`. The parity config has `retries: CI?1:0`.
proposed: Make one exported `specSeconds()` and import it in both tools.
effect: Locality. Latent until retries are turned on.

title: next-ticket prints the wrong claim command, and its comment read is capped
problem: `printDetail` always prints `gh issue edit --add-label in-progress`. For the implement route, queue.md prescribes `npm run queue:claim`. Separately, the comment fetch stops at `per_page=100` with no pagination.
proposed: Print the route's own claim command, and paginate (`--paginate`).
effect: Removes a doc/tool contradiction.

title: ios-device.yml's push path filter misses native inputs
problem: The filter lists package.json, the lock, app.json, assets/images and the workflow itself. It misses `modules/` (murlan-diagnostics, murlan-audio-session, murlan-orientation), `plugins/` (withSwiftUIFilters.js) and `patches/`. So a native change on main never rebuilds the dev-client IPA, and ios-device.mjs installs the newest successful build, which carries a stale fingerprint.
proposed: Add the three globs.
effect: Device runs test the code that is on main.

title: `HARD_FACTOR = 3` is defined three times
problem: RULES.md rule 46 states it as one owner ruling, but each copy has its own `<= 3` pin, so the copies can drift apart. `RATIO` already shows the right shape: one export, imported by budget-gate.
proposed: Export it once from e2e-budget.mjs, import it in the other two, and keep a single pin.
effect: Locality.

title: build-court-art `CROP` duplicates `COURT_ART_BOX`
problem: The two are kept equal only by a "keep in step" comment. bake-card-art.mjs already imports from cardFaceModel.ts, so the import path exists.
proposed: Import `COURT_ART_BOX`.
effect: One owner.

title: diagnostics collector port 5099 is a literal in three places
problem: The three literals are not tied to each other. The E2E mark, by contrast, is pinned by e2eBuildMark.test.ts:22.
proposed: Export it once from lib and have both scripts import it, or add a pin.
effect: Locality.

title: `server:dev` and `server:prod` use POSIX env prefixes
problem: `NODE_ENV=x cmd` fails under npm's default cmd shell on Windows, which is the owner's machine. README.md:18 tells developers to run `server:dev`, and there is no .npmrc setting `script-shell`. Production on Linux is unaffected.
proposed: Set NODE_ENV inside the entry point, or use `node --env-file`.
effect: The documented dev command works on the dev machine.

title: checks.md:96-97 describes the dispatch gate backwards
problem: The doc says the gate refuses a dispatch off an `agent/<n>-` or `claude/<n>-` branch. The gate actually allows only those branches.
proposed: Reword it.
effect: Correct doc.

title: Small loop-test defects
problem: a duplicate name hides which test failed, cleanup leaks on failure, the fixed sleep is flake-prone, and the global mock is a missing seam.
proposed: as listed in each item.
effect: four small fixes.

title: `result-schema.json` lets extra fields through; a test does that check by hand
problem: the schema has `required` but no `additionalProperties: false`. The test re-implements that rule over queue.md's printed examples only, so a model emitting a stray field in a real session is accepted.
proposed: add `"additionalProperties": false` and drop the manual loop (keep the required check).
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Small shell hardening
problem: (a) `sort | tail -1` is lexicographic, so `build-tools/9.0.0` would beat `34.0.0` and `100.x` loses to `35.x`; use `sort -V`. (b) `$title` goes into a double-quoted jq string from `$workflow`; only `ios.yml` and `maestro.yml` pass today, but `--arg t "$title"` and `select(.title == $t)` removes the quoting hazard. (c) gitleaks-scan.sh has no `-e`/`-u`, and it relies on its callers noticing the exit status.
proposed: `sort -V`. (b) `$title` goes into a double-quoted jq string from `$workflow`; only `ios.yml` and `maestro.yml` pass today, but `--arg t "$title"` and `select(.title == $t)` removes the quoting hazard. (c) gitleaks-scan.sh has no `-e`/`-u`, and it relies on its callers noticing the exit status.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: `skills-lock.json` lists seven skills, only one is installed, and nothing reads it
problem: six entries (`find-skills`, `frontend-design`, `next-best-practices`, `radon-mcp`, `rnrepo`, `typegpu`) have no directory in `.claude/skills`. `next-best-practices` is a Next.js skill in an Expo app. The only reference to the file in SRC is the audit workflow's scope list (`.claude/workflows/audit.mjs:255`).
proposed: either regenerate it from the installed skills or delete it.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: In-process modules are called through subprocesses and stdout protocols
problem: `queue-loop.mjs:1436-1440` runs `node claim.mjs` and parses `claimed.split("\t")[2]` and `err.stdout.split("\t").at(-1)`, even though `claim(number, title, run, tracker)` (claim.mjs:87-117) is importable and already returns `{branch, cwd, won, why}`. `queue-loop.mjs:580-582, 617` remove worktrees with `npm run worktrees:remove`, going through the `sh` shell path on Windows, even though `workspace.removeWorktree(target, {force, git})` (workspace.mjs:154-202) is importable. The two exports are both named …
proposed: call `claim()` and `removeWorktree()` in-process from the workspace port. Delete the source-text pin and the tab-protocol parsing; the subprocess CLIs stay for by-hand use.
effect: four brittle scans fewer.

title: Issue-read trust policy lives in `brief.mjs` and comes in three shapes
problem: `brief.mjs:45-70` (`TRUSTED_SELECT` jq, `readIssue`, `untrustedRead`, `apiMethod`) is imported by guard-bash.mjs:19 and next-ticket.mjs:3. That is the subagent-prompt module serving as the tracker's policy. `trustedComments` (loop-derive.mjs:328-333, `authorAssociation`) and `trusted()` (next-ticket.mjs:9-11, `author_association`) re-express the same rule.
proposed: move these into `github.mjs` (F3); brief imports from there.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.
notes: Not re-verified by a slice reviewer.

title: The agent-check cache is an implicit file interface and self-reported gate evidence
problem: The writer is `agent-check.mjs:178-180, 237`; the reader is `loop-gate.mjs:47`, which rebuilds the path `join(gitDir, "agent-check-cache.json")` itself and shares the `{pass, head, clean, deferred}` schema only by convention. loopGate.test.ts:435 writes the file directly. `buildPassed` (loop-gate.mjs:36-52) trusts a file the gated session can write with Bash.
proposed: `agent-check.mjs` exports `passFor(cwd, head)` so the path and schema have one owner, and document `--build` as advisory.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.
notes: 06-tooling: partly wrong. The schema is shared (loop-gate imports cleanPassFor from agent-check); only the cache path is duplicated (loop-gate.mjs:47, agent-check.mjs:179), an XS fix rather than a schema split.

title: Guard hooks fail open silently, which makes `onFailure: "block"` dead config
problem: `guard-write.mjs:41-43` and `guard-agent-model.mjs:66-68` wrap everything in `catch { process.exit(0) }`, which includes `checkoutRoot(cwd)` throwing (cli.mjs:70-71). They print nothing. guard-bash.mjs:427-431 also allows on an unreadable payload, but at least prints to stderr.
proposed: let a parse failure exit non-zero (or deny) and keep `exit 0` only for "no file_path"; at least write to stderr as guard-bash does.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.
notes: ADR-0010 sets guards to onFailure: "block"; failing open makes that config dead, so the fix enforces the ADR.

title: "The change" is computed five different ways
problem: `agent-check.mjs:33-51`: `origin/main...HEAD` + tracked status, excluding untracked. `related-tests.mjs:60-66`: `origin/main...HEAD` + `HEAD` + untracked included. This runs inside agent-check's `native:related` step, so a scratch file can pick tests while the subject says untracked files are not a change.
proposed: `changeSet(cwd, {base, untracked})` in one module (cli.mjs or a new `change.mjs`).
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: gh/git wrappers outside tools/loop
problem: `scripts/await-run.mjs:15-21`, `tools/ci/await-artifact.mjs:52`, `tools/ci/ios-wall.mjs:57`, `tools/ci/budget-gate.mjs:131-132` (re-states the 64 MB `MAX_BUFFER`), `tools/ci/nativeScope.mjs:54`, `tools/ci/e2e-budget.mjs:17`, `scripts/ios-device.mjs:99-103`. cli.test.ts's "no git or gh outside cli.mjs" scan covers only `tools/loop/*` (cli.test.ts:116). Each of these already takes an injected function, so leverage is low.
proposed: import `cli.mjs`'s `gh`/`git` (it is deliberately dependency-light, cli.mjs:1-3) and widen the scan.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: The e2e port literal is in four places, and the process-table module sits in the loop
problem: `5199` appears at tools/ci/e2ePort.mjs:17 (`BASE_PORT`), scripts/e2e-server.mjs:32, tools/loop/reap.mjs:14 and tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts:25. reap clears only `E2E_PORT ?? 5199`, while `chooseE2ePort` may hand out 5199-5218 (e2ePort.mjs:18, 32-49).
proposed: export `BASE_PORT` once and import it everywhere. Move the process-table and port functions to `scripts/lib/processes.mjs`, shared by reap and e2ePort.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Minor shallow items
problem: Minor shallow items: three trimmed-git micro-wrappers (loop-derive.mjs:18, loop-gate.mjs:31-33, brief.mjs:25-31, plus agent-check.mjs:174-176), `scripts/dev-stack.mjs:95` spawning a node process to sleep, and a module-level mutable `openPrs` cache in next-ticket.mjs:176-180.
proposed: Offer `git(cwd).lines(args)`/`.text(args)` from cli.mjs, use in-process `Atomics.wait` for the sleep, and let the `openPrs` cache disappear into tooling-F3's `github.prs()`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: queue-loop resolves paths against the cwd despite its HERE/ROOT contract
problem: The HERE/ROOT comment at :89-92 says paths resolve from the script. They do not: `queueLoopArgs` reads `.claude/commands/queue.md` relative to the cwd (:240). `defaultStamp` reads relative paths (:269-276).
proposed: Route all three through `ROOT`.
effect: The interface matches its stated contract.

title: checks.md documents an `await-run --pr` mode that does not exist
problem: The doc says that with `--pr <n>`, a passed run that is over budget also exits 1. In fact `runArgs` rejects every non-numeric argument, and the test asserts `runArgs(["--pr","7","1"]) === null`, so the command prints usage and exits 2.
proposed: Delete the paragraph. The budget gate already covers over-budget runs.
effect: The doc stops promising a check that runs nowhere.

title: diagnostics gates restate each scenario's sample count
problem: Each count is written twice, so changing a scenario's iterations reds the gate for a reason unrelated to performance.
proposed: Export a `samples` constant from each scenario and import it in the verdict. `lampVariants` already does this with `LAMP_SWAY.samples`.
effect: One owner per count.

title: failure reporting to the tracker is copied about four times, and two soak jobs share one issue
problem: The same "find the open labelled issue, else create it, then comment" logic is copied about four times. The two soak.yml jobs share the `soak` label and its one-open-issue lookup, so offline-match failures and socket-soak failures comment on each other's issue. audio-soak.yml does not report at all.
proposed: Use report-device-run.sh, or one composite action, as the single implementation, with a per-job label or title key.
effect: Locality. Failures land on the right issue.
